title: Gregor's Ledger
summary: Read from the back, Gregor's ledger keeps one page for each autumn of the Tithe. He did not trust the names to ink: each is a sum, and every sum is an account in the honest front pages.
question: Match each autumn's sum to its account in the front pages. Whose name did the Tithe fall to, year by year?

clues.note: One page for each autumn of the Tithe, five of them, in Gregor's careful merchant's hand. The fifth is struck through so hard the nib tore the page.

clues.text: The honest front of the book: flour, lamp oil, nails, seed grain on credit. The accounts, as written: Ashby, seed grain, thirty copper. The forge, boots for the smith's boy, sixteen copper. The Rusty Nail, ale casks, thirty-six copper. Marlow, lamp oil through the winter, twenty-one copper. The chapel, candles, eight copper. Brand, a roof mended, twenty-six copper. Fenn, flour, thirteen copper.

lines.cipher: Year five: thirteen copper, struck through

hints.text: A merchant who hides a name writes it where he would never look twice: in what the family owes.
The smith has no family in the book. The forge does, and a boy's boots.

solved_summary: read Gregor's ledger back from its sums to five names, one for each autumn of the Tithe
